assumptions: Capacity is per plant AND product per week (plants.csv has one row per plant-product); each order consumes the capacity of its own product line only.
An order ships on day 4 (0=Mon) of the week its last unit is built; arrival = ship date + transit_days. Production lead time inside a week is not modelled.
Orders are never split across plants; a large order may be built over several weeks at the same plant (earliest-deadline-first) and ships when its last unit is built.
Landed cost = production + energy (kWh x price from energy_price_per_kwh column) + transport + duty; duty base = exworks.
Carbon = energy_kwh_per_unit x carbon_kg_per_kwh + transport carbon_kg_per_unit, times qty.
Weights cost 0.7 / carbon 0.3; each normalised by the sum of per-order minima so 1.0 = 'best possible' on that axis.
Priority: serve every order > minimise late orders > minimise late days > weighted cost/carbon.
Overlapping capacity events on the same plant and day combine by 'sum_capped'; a partial-week event reduces capacity by the share of affected days.
limitations: Duty rates and transit days assumed constant over the horizon.
No weekly variation in carbon intensity (no such column in the schema).
No inventory/holding cost for building early.
Capacity unit assumed to be 'units of that product per week'.
